log: LOOP 193  THE 44-GENE SEAM: a mechanism, or a bookkeeping overlap?
PREDECLARED: the planned substrate-supply test CANNOT be built and the docstring says
why before offering an alternative -- acetyl-CoA in K562 is ONE number, constant across
genes, so it cannot predict which gene carries a mark within one cell type, and every
mark measurement here is one cell type. That is loop 185's Z6 lesson one level up, and
this time the quantity really is constant, so the test really is inert. What is asked
instead is whether the 44 regulate metabolism more than degree-matched other regulators
(R2) and whether the coupling is specific to their own chemistry (R3), both at z > 3.0 against 2000 draws.
R1 DOES THE SEAM REPRODUCE?
recomputed 44 bridge genes; census recorded 44
ARID4B, ASH1L, CLOCK, CNOT4, CREBBP, CTBP1, DBP, DNMT1, DNMT3A, DNMT3B, DNMT3L, DOT1L, ENO1, EP300 ...
R1 PASS -- the seam reproduces at 44, so what follows is about the genes the census counted
control pool: 1,133 curated regulators that are NOT modelled enzymes
R2 DO THE 44 REGULATE METABOLISM MORE THAN OTHER REGULATORS DO?
bridge out-degree: median 9, range 1-582
fraction of targets that are modelled enzymes: observed 0.2121
degree-matched null 0.1383 +/- 0.0294 over 2000 draws  ->  z +2.5
R2 FAIL -- z +2.5; at matched out-degree the bridge genes are no more metabolic in their targeting than any other regulator, so dual membership does not come with a regulatory preference
R3 IS IT THEIR OWN CHEMISTRY?
acetyl: 12 species ids
sam: 2 species ids
nad: 6 species ids
18 of 44 bridge genes touch acetyl-CoA, SAM or NAD+ in their own reactions
fraction of targets sharing the writer's own substrate: observed 0.0614
R3 PASS -- the coupling is specific to the chemistry each writer performs (z +10.1), which is what a mechanism would look like
R4 THE STRANGER SWAP
AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS GATE COULD NOT MOVE, which is recorded rather than
quietly repaired. It swapped target sets among the 44 and compared the GROUP MEAN of
per-gene metabolic fractions -- a quantity that is invariant under a permutation of
which gene holds which set, because the multiset of fractions is unchanged. Real and
swapped both came back 0.2121, exactly. That is gate_guard's own family two: a null
arithmetically incapable of changing the statistic it is meant to destroy.
R3's statistic is different and a swap DOES bite it, because it depends on the
PAIRING between a writer's own substrate class and its targets, which permuting
breaks. So the swap is run against R3, which is also the gate that passed -- a
passing result with no working control is what this project does not ship.
the swap changes 95% of the target sets (capable)
R3 statistic: real 0.0614, swapped 0.0027, null 0.0048
real excess +0.0566 against swapped excess -0.0021
R4 PASS -- breaking the pairing between a writer and its targets collapses the chemistry-specific enrichment (0.0614 -> 0.0027), so it belongs to which writer has which targets
R5 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
The substrate-supply question is UNANSWERED, not answered. It needs mark measurements
across cells differing in metabolic state, and nothing on this disk has that. A later
loop that finds such data should not treat this loop as having tested it.
CollecTRI is literature-curated, and chromatin writers are among the most studied
proteins in the genome. If their targets look metabolic it may be because their
metabolic targets are the ones people looked for. Degree matching controls for how
BROAD a regulator is, not for what its literature is about.
Human-GEM assigns these writers reactions because their chemistry is in the model, so
'is a modelled enzyme' is partly a statement about the model's scope. The seam is 44
genes in THIS model, not a fact about the cell.
A pass at R2 with a fail at R3 would say the bridge genes prefer metabolic targets
without preferring their own chemistry, which is a coupling but not a mechanism. The
two gates are separate so that combination can be reported rather than blurred.
